## Problem

`tests/**` resolve `@worklog/shared` through the package `exports` map to the **built** output (`packages/shared/dist/`), which is gitignored. A checkout whose `packages/shared/dist` predates a change under `packages/shared/src` therefore exercises the OLD shared code, and the full suite reports failures for work that is already correct and merged.

Each implement worktree builds its own `packages/shared/dist`, so the dev-push gate (which tests the pushed commit in a clean/wt checkout) can be green while the long-lived main checkout stays stale — the failure then reappears in the main checkout, in audit runs and in any agent session that runs the suite from there.

## Evidence (2026-11-08)

- Main checkout `packages/shared/dist/database/work-items.js` was built 2026-11-07T13:46Z; commit `36d965a4` (WL-0MW8078CA006Q2P7, 2026-11-08T21:22Z) changed `packages/shared/src/database/work-items.ts` to add cascade delete attribution.
- A fresh full-suite run at dev HEAD `3dad96d4` (clean tree, `run_tests.py --type full --scope full --force`) failed 3 tests in `tests/cli/delete-reason.test.ts`: expected `cascade from <parent-id>: sweeping subtree`, received `sweeping subtree` (the pre-change behaviour).
- After `npm run build` in the same checkout the identical suite was green: 344 files / 4825 tests passed, 0 failed.

## Desired outcome

Make the mismatch visible instead of silent, e.g. any of:

- a guard that fails the suite (or `run_tests.py`) with an actionable message when `packages/shared/src` is newer than `packages/shared/dist`;
- a build step in the test runner for the workspace shared package (cost-aware, cache-keyed);
- a documented, enforced rebuild precondition for full-suite evidence in `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md` / the test-skill reference.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A full-suite run in a checkout with a `packages/shared/dist` older than `packages/shared/src` either rebuilds it or fails immediately with an actionable message naming the rebuild command.
2. The guard/behaviour is covered by a test (stale and fresh dist cases).
3. `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md` (and the test-skill reference if behaviour lives in the runner) document the requirement.
4. The full project test suite passes.

## Impact

Agents and audits stop chasing phantom test failures caused by a stale local workspace build, so a red suite once again means the code is actually broken.
data.title: Full-suite runs in an existing checkout silently use a stale @worklog/shared build

# Host-wide release barrier while a release runs

## Problem statement

The Code Freeze marker (`.worklog/code-freeze.json`) is **per worklog root**, but the host dispatch budget ledger is **machine-scoped**. During a release in project A the dispatcher skips new implement/audit dispatch for project A only; another project on the same host (or the coordination leader's registered-root sweep) can still start implement/audit panes while the release's own audit/test subprocesses are saturating the machine.

The release-dispatch-budget evaluation (WL-0MW7YIBG70021YI3) concluded a dedicated release *budget slot* is not warranted (the ledger counts dispatched panes, not release subprocesses), but identified this cross-project scope mismatch as the real residual gap.

## Proposed change

Introduce a machine-scoped release-in-progress marker (in `machine-coordination.ts`, alongside the budget ledger — reusing the same coordination dir/lock) that the dispatcher honours for **implement and audit** tiers on **every root**, so a release anywhere on the host pauses new heavy dispatch everywhere. In-progress panes keep running; plan/intake prep still dispatches (matching the per-root freeze split-by-skill).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A machine-scoped release marker is written/cleared by the release process with the same atomic + fail-closed semantics as `code-freeze.json`.
2. While the marker is active, the dispatcher skips new implement/audit dispatch for every root (both the direct path and the coordination-leader sweep), with a neutral reason token that does not arm the no-candidate cooldown.
3. In-progress implement/audit panes are not interrupted; plan/intake (including critical prep) still dispatches.
4. The per-root code-freeze gate remains and composes with the host barrier (belt-and-braces).
5. The ledger's admission path stays unchanged for budget accounting; this barrier is a separate, earlier gate.
6. Documentation and tests pin the behaviour.

## Related work

- WL-0MW7YIBG70021YI3 — Evaluate budgets (parent evaluation; recommends this follow-up)
- WL-0MSBU4KMA004PKSR — Code Freeze (per-root marker)
- WL-0MVXWQFGV000D2AB — Host-wide concurrency budget
- WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB — Generalise host dispatch budget to any work item type

# F1 — Kind-generalised config & ledger

First implementation slice of WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB: generalise `HostBudgetKind`
to every `DowntimeSkillKind` member, make `budget.json` a map over kinds
(absent kind ⇒ uncapped) with legacy `max*` key read-compat, keep the
`implement: 2` / `audit: 1` defaults, and generalise the env overrides to
`HERDR_HOST_MAX_<KIND>`. No admissions change yet (that is F2).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `HostBudgetKind` covers all five `DowntimeSkillKind` members (`implement`,
  `audit`, `plan`, `intake`, `risk-effort`); ledger entry validation and
  `HostBudgetCounts` accept every kind.
- `budget.json` accepts kind-named keys (`{ "implement": 2, "audit": 1,
  "plan": 3, ... }`); a kind absent from the file is **uncapped** (no default
  cap invented) and `maxImplement` / `maxAudit` legacy keys are still honoured
  (read-compat), so existing operator files keep their meaning (AC3).
- Defaults stay `implement: 2`, `audit: 1`; `0` remains the per-kind kill
  switch, clamped to `0..HOST_BUDGET_MAX (32)`.
- Env overrides generalised: `HERDR_HOST_MAX_<KIND>` for all five kinds, with
  the two existing names (`HERDR_HOST_MAX_IMPLEMENT` / `HERDR_HOST_MAX_AUDIT`)
  still valid; malformed values keep the file/default figure with a warning.
- The fixed two-key `DEFAULT_HOST_BUDGET_CONFIG` shape is replaced by the kind
  map; no other module's behaviour changes in this slice.
- `HOST_BUDGET_ENV_KEYS` maps every kind to its env name; module header updated.

- **Traceability (covers parent AC1 — any kind configurable):** `budget.json` accepts a cap for every dispatch kind (`implement`, `audit`, `plan`, `intake`, `risk-effort`). A cap set for any kind is enforced at admission (refuse when live >= cap) on both dispatcher paths (direct and coordination leader), with `0` remaining the per-kind kill switch.
- **Traceability (covers parent AC2 — absent = unlimited):** a kind not explicitly present in the budget config is unlimited: admission never refuses it on budget grounds, it is never counted against any cap, and its dispatches are not recorded in the ledger (no reserve/release bookkeeping for uncapped kinds). No default cap is invented for unconfigured kinds.
- **Traceability (covers parent AC3 — existing budgets preserved):** the default stays `implement: 2`, `audit: 1`, and an operator's existing `budget.json` values keep their meaning and enforcement (same refusal behaviour, same kill switch) — the generalisation must not change or silently drop configured caps.
## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts` — kind type, config schema,
  defaults, env overrides, ledger normalisation, counts
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.test.ts` / `.fixtures.ts` — updated
  config/ledger matrix
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — env/config docs (final wording in F6)

## Minimal Implementation

1. Extend `HostBudgetKind` / `HostBudgetEntry.kind` / `HostBudgetCounts` /
   `HostBudgetConfig` to all five kinds.
2. Rewrite `parseBudgetConfig` / `resolveBudgetConfig` / `applyBudgetEnvOverrides`
   over a kind map with legacy `max*` read-compat and absent-⇒-uncapped.
3. Replace `DEFAULT_HOST_BUDGET_CONFIG` and `HOST_BUDGET_ENV_KEYS` with the kind
   map; keep `clampHostBudget` / `HOST_BUDGET_MAX` unchanged.
4. Generalise ledger normalisation (`normalizeLedgerEntry` kind checks) and the
   counting reductions' statically-typed counts.
5. Update unit tests; run the changed-scope test gate.

## Dependencies

- T1 (WL-0MWF33QKQ002H17E) — the test matrix pins the target semantics.

## Deliverables

Kind-generalised config + ledger; operator files and defaults preserved;
uncapped kinds recognised end-to-end.

# F2 — Generic admission + audit-only over-hold

Second implementation slice of WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB: make admission one generic
path for every capped kind on BOTH dispatcher paths (direct and coordination
leader), keep the counting asymmetry audit-only (`freshCount` over-hold for
audit; `liveCount` live-pane release for every other kind), and unify refusal
tokens on `host-budget-<kind>` (removing the `maxAudit: 1` → `audit-host-saturated`
special-case). Uncapped kinds admit without reservation and touch no ledger.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `admitHostDispatch` resolves the kind's cap from the generalised config:
  absent ⇒ admit WITHOUT reservation (no reserve/release/confirm bookkeeping);
  present ⇒ existing live-count admission; `0` ⇒ refuse with `0/0`.
- Counting asymmetry preserved: only `audit` uses `freshCount` (slot held from
  reservation until a release point or the 2 h stale window, no live-pane
  requirement); `implement`, `plan`, `intake`, `risk-effort` use `liveCount`
  (live-pane release, pane-derived freshness).
- Admission is enforced on BOTH dispatcher paths: the direct path
  (`dispatchClaimedTier` in `downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts`) and the
  coordination-leader path (`downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` /
  `coordination-batch.ts`) call the same generic `admitHostDispatch` for every
  capped kind and skip it for uncapped kinds.
- Refusal tokens unified: `host-budget-<kind>` for the kind's cap refusal;
  `audit-host-saturated` special-case removed (the audit tier reports
  `host-budget-audit` at every cap including the `maxAudit: 1` default).
- Fail-closed semantics unchanged: unreadable ledger ⇒ `host-budget-unknown` +
  repair from live panes; `no-coordination-dir` ⇒ admit; lock/IO failure ⇒ refuse.
- `kindOf`/`entriesFromLivePanes` reconstruct any kind's pane (not just
  implement/audit) for the repair path.

- **Traceability (covers parent AC1 — any kind configurable):** `budget.json` accepts a cap for every dispatch kind (`implement`, `audit`, `plan`, `intake`, `risk-effort`). A cap set for any kind is enforced at admission (refuse when live >= cap) on both dispatcher paths (direct and coordination leader), with `0` remaining the per-kind kill switch.
- **Traceability (covers parent AC4 — counting asymmetry preserved, audit-only):** only `audit` keeps the over-hold semantics: it counts fresh ledger entries with **no** live-pane requirement (`freshCount` — slot held from reservation until a release point fires or the 2 h stale window). Every **other** kind counts only fresh entries whose pane is in the machine-wide live pane list (`liveCount`), so its slot frees when the pane leaves the live list.
## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts` — generic admission,
  refusal tokens, audit over-hold, repair
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts` — admission choke
  point (`dispatchClaimedTier`) + failure release for all kinds
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` —
  `dispatchFromCoordination` admission
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `admitHostDispatch` seam (kind passthrough)
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.admission.test.ts` /
  `coordination-dispatch.test.ts` / `downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts`

## Minimal Implementation

1. Generalise `admitHostDispatch` to look up the kind's cap/absence.
2. Add the no-reservation fast path for uncapped kinds.
3. Remove the `audit-host-saturated` special-case in `readAuditBudgetState` /
   `admitAuditLegacy`; unify on `host-budget-audit`.
4. Generalise `kindOf` / `entriesFromLivePanes` for pane-title reconstruction.
5. Widen `releaseHostBudgetForFailure` and the admission call in
   `dispatchClaimedTier` to all kinds (skip still for uncapped — release is a
   no-op for kinds that never reserve).
6. Update admission/dispatch/coordination tests; run the changed-scope gate.

## Dependencies

- F1 (WL-0MWF33ZB0000RC88) — generalised config/ledger.
- T1 (WL-0MWF33QKQ002H17E) — the test matrix pins admission semantics.

## Deliverables

One generic admission path; audit-only over-hold; unified tokens; both
dispatcher paths enforce caps for every configured kind.
data.title: Generic admission + audit-only over-hold

# F3 — Legacy marker & token removal

Third implementation slice of WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB: delete the retired
`active-audit` marker readers and the synthetic legacy-marker entry count, and
remove the `audit-host-saturated` compat token and fixed two-key env overrides —
no backward-compatibility shims, per AC5. A repo-wide scan confirms no
references to the removed symbols remain, and the module headers / F6 contract
wording are updated to match.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `readActiveAuditMarker` and `isHostAuditActive` (machine-coordination.ts) are
  deleted; `legacyActiveAuditCount` and the synthetic legacy-marker entry count
  in `freshCount` / `auditDisplayCount` / `reduceMarkerCounts` are removed —
  no compat shims or read-compat paths remain.
- The `audit-host-saturated` token is gone: `HOST_BUDGET_AUDIT_SATURATED_REFUSAL`,
  the `maxAudit: 1` special-case in `readAuditBudgetState`, and every
  `'audit-host-saturated'` literal in dispatch/constants/contract/types are
  deleted; the audit tier reports `host-budget-audit` at every cap.
- Fixed two-key env overrides (`HERDR_HOST_MAX_IMPLEMENT` / `HERDR_HOST_MAX_AUDIT`
  as the ONLY keys) are gone — the generalised `HERDR_HOST_MAX_<KIND>` map (F1)
  is the single source of the env override vocabulary.
- The F6 doc carve-out text (plan/intake/risk-effort "out of scope") is removed
  from `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and the module headers of all affected
  files (host-dispatch-budget.ts, admission.ts, machine-coordination.ts,
  dispatch.ts, dispatch-claims.ts, types/contract/constants).
- Repo-wide scan (grep) confirms zero references to the removed symbols
  (`readActiveAuditMarker`, `isHostAuditActive`, `legacyActiveAuditCount`,
  `audit-host-saturated`, `reduceMarkerCounts` synthetic counting) in
  `packages/herdr/src` and `docs/`.

- **AC5 traceability:** legacy code removed (no backward compatibility): the following are deleted, not kept behind compat shims: active-audit marker readers, synthetic count, audit-host-saturated, two-kind type and default shape, F6 carve-out.

- `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.ts` — delete marker readers/types
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts` — drop legacy count + synthetic entry
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts` — drop saturated token
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.ts` / `.dispatch-claims.ts` /
  `.constants.ts` / `.types.ts` / `.dispatch-contract.ts` / `.orchestrator-dispatch.ts`
  — token vocabulary updates
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` / `downtime-log-budget.ts` — reason vocab
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — F6 carve-out + removal-schedule wording
- Tests: `host-dispatch-budget*.test.ts`, `host-budget-status.test.ts`,
  `downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts`, `machine-coordination.test.ts`

## Minimal Implementation

1. Delete the marker readers/constants from machine-coordination.ts.
2. Drop `legacyActiveAuditCount` and the synthetic-entry additions in
   `freshCount`/`auditDisplayCount`; remove `reduceMarkerCounts`'s marker
   special-casing (keep the freshness rule for audit directly).
3. Remove `HOST_BUDGET_AUDIT_SATURATED_REFUSAL` and its dispatch literals.
4. Update the decision-log/constants/contract vocabulary and the F6 docs wording.
5. Update affected tests; add/keep a repo-wide reference scan; run the gate.

## Dependencies

- F2 (WL-0MWF34932000SNTX) — token unification lands before the compat token is deleted.
- T1 (WL-0MWF33QKQ002H17E) — the matrix asserts the legacy surface is gone.

## Deliverables

Legacy marker surface deleted; unified `host-budget-*` vocabulary; clean
repo-wide scan; updated module headers and contract wording.

# F4 — Interactive gate for all kinds

Fourth implementation slice of WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB: generalise the hand-fired
over-quota gate so a `/skill:<kind>` dispatch for ANY capped kind consults the
same ledger/cap and prompts on over-quota exactly as implement/audit do today;
uncapped kinds skip the gate entirely (no prompt, no reservation, no ledger
entry). `budgetKindForAgentCommand` covers all five kinds.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `budgetKindForAgentCommand` maps `/skill:plan`, `/skill:intake`,
  `/skill:risk-effort` (and the existing implement/audit families) to their
  `HostBudgetKind`; prefix matching unchanged.
- For a CAPPED kind, `prepareInteractiveAgentDispatch` reads the kind's cap/
  ledger, prompts on over-quota (cancel ⇒ no claim/pane/entry; proceed ⇒ reserve
  with `override: { by: 'user' }`), and skips the prompt below quota — identical
  behaviour to implement/audit today (AC6).
- For an UNCAPPED kind, the gate short-circuits: no quota check, no prompt, no
  reservation, no ledger entry — the claim path proceeds unchanged.
- `scheduled` prompts (not a work-item kind) stay outside the budget entirely.
- The dialog renders the kind (headline/live/max) generically for any capped
  kind; `host-budget-dialog` and the TUI accept any kind.

- **Traceability (covers parent AC6 — interactive over-quota gate generalised):** a hand-fired `/skill:<kind>` dispatch for any capped kind consults the same ledger/cap and prompts on over-quota, exactly as implement/audit do today (`budgetKindForAgentCommand` generalised to all kinds).
## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.interactive.ts` — kind mapping + gate
- `packages/herdr/src/host-budget-dialog.ts` / `host-budget-dialog-tui.ts` — prompt rendering
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — wiring of `prepareInteractiveAgentDispatch`
- Tests: `host-dispatch-budget.interactive.test.ts`, `host-budget-dialog.test.ts`,
  `host-budget-dialog-tui.test.ts`

## Minimal Implementation

1. Generalise `budgetKindForAgentCommand` to all five kinds.
2. In `prepareInteractiveAgentDispatch`, resolve the kind's cap: absent ⇒
   claim-through (uncapped); present ⇒ existing read/prompt/reserve flow with a
   generic kind.
3. Generalise `readTierCount`'s kind branches to the generic live-count rule
   (audit keeps the display count).
4. Generalise `HostBudgetPromptRequest` / dialog headline text to carry any kind.
5. Update interactive/dialog/TUI tests; run the changed-scope gate.

## Dependencies

- F1 (WL-0MWF33ZB0000RC88) — kind-generalised config (cap lookup, absence).
- T1 (WL-0MWF33QKQ002H17E) — gate expectations pinned in the matrix.

## Deliverables

Hand-fired over-quota gate for every capped kind; uncapped kinds bypass the
budget with zero bookkeeping.
data.title: Interactive gate for all kinds

# F5 — Observability per configured kind

Fifth implementation slice of WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB: generalise the observability
surfaces — worklist header counter, stderr skip line and decision-log tokens —
to report live/max **per configured (capped) kind**; uncapped kinds never
appear in any surface and can never produce a budget refusal token (AC7).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `readHostBudgetStatus` / `summariseHostBudget` produce per-kind live/max for
  every CONFIGURED kind ONLY; uncapped kinds are never listed.
- `hostBudgetStatusText` renders the header segment from the generalised status
  (e.g. `[budget: implement 1/2 · audit 0/1 · plan 0/3]`), with the exact
  existing implement/audit format preserved when those are the only capped kinds.
- `hostBudgetSkipLine` names the kind for every `host-budget-<kind>` token
  (live/max figures included); an uncapped kind never produces a skip line.
- Decision-log/refusal-token vocabulary is fully generalised: `host-budget-*`
  tokens exist per kind and `host-budget-unknown` keeps its tier-neutral wording;
  a repo scan shows no fixed two-kind-only rendering paths remain.

- **Traceability (covers parent AC7 — observability generalised):** the worklist header counter, stderr skip line and decision-log tokens report live/max **per configured kind** (any capped kind), never for uncapped kinds; an uncapped kind can never produce a budget refusal token.
## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/host-budget-status.ts` — status pairing + header/skip-line text
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — header segment consumption
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` / `downtime-log-budget.ts` /
  `downtime-worker.constants.ts` — decision-token vocabulary
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts` — skip-line write
- Tests: `host-budget-status.test.ts`, `host-budget-observability.test.ts`,
  `downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts`, `index.test.ts`

## Minimal Implementation

1. Generalise `HostBudgetStatus` / `summariseHostBudget` to a per-kind record
   (only configured kinds present).
2. Rework `hostBudgetStatusText` to iterate the configured kinds.
3. Generalise `TIER_LABEL_BY_REASON` / `hostBudgetSkipLine` to all kinds.
4. Update decision-token vocabulary and any fixed two-kind rendering paths.
5. Update observability/worklist/dialog tests; run the changed-scope gate.

## Dependencies

- F2 (WL-0MWF34932000SNTX) — unified tokens + generic admission evidence.
- F4 (WL-0MWF34P5G006QOOX) — interactive gate surfaces the same counts.
- T1 (WL-0MWF33QKQ002H17E) — observability expectations pinned in the matrix.

## Deliverables

Per-kind observability; uncapped kinds invisible on every surface; no budget
token noise for unconfigured kinds.
data.title: Observability per configured kind

data.description:
# Downtime offers: fill empty buckets from the rest of the project backlog, not just the visible list

## Problem statement

The dispatcher can only dispatch what an instance *offers*. Each herdr instance computes its offers in `computeMostImportantItem` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination.ts`) by partitioning its **sprint-view window** — the live `browseItemCount`, currently 20 items — into the `implement` / `audit` / `prep` buckets.

The per-bucket nominees are strictly window-only. From the tier-aware offers work (WL-0MWDDHQON0015T3P, AC3): "A bucket empty in the window nominates nothing and the window is never widened to fill it". The whole-backlog extension that already exists (`fetchExtendedHerdrItems` / `fetchWholeBacklogTail`, WL-0MW9XS0XR007K1TH — "selection must consider every work item, not just the sprint view") feeds only the *single* legacy offer, never the nominee buckets.

Result on 13 Nov 2026 (live coordination file, `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-coordination.json`):

```
AI_Hell              offers=[implement, audit, prep]   ← 3 buckets
ContextHub           offers=[implement, audit, prep]   ← 3 buckets
tce-the-rising       offers=[audit]                    ← 1 bucket
SorraAgents          offers=[audit]                    ← 1 bucket
tce-main-street      offers=[audit]                    ← 1 bucket
Tableau-Card-Engine  offers=[audit]                    ← 1 bucket
```

tce-the-rising's ranked head, for example, is three `plan_complete` items followed by 16 `in_review` audits, and the first two plan items are filtered out (a 24 h dispatched-marker and a live pane). The window's audit bucket therefore fills, the other two buckets nominate nothing, and the leader has no prep or implement offer to fall through to when the audit is refused. Its backlog beyond item 20 — and every other ready item in the project — is invisible to the dispatcher.

## Desired change

When the visible list yields no nominee for a bucket, keep walking the SAME canonical ranking deeper into the project's backlog until each bucket has a nominee (or the backlog is exhausted). The visible window is a rendering bound, not a dispatch bound — the same principle already applied to the single-offer path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The nominee scan is no longer window-only: for each `implement` / `audit` / `prep` bucket without a nominee after the visible window is scanned, the scan continues through the geometric whole-backlog extension (reuse `fetchExtendedHerdrItems` / `fetchWholeBacklogTail`, `DOWNTIME_DISPATCH_EXTEND_MAX` growth and its round cap) until that bucket has a nominee or the tail is exhausted.
- The extension is a WINDOW WIDENING of the same canonical ranking (`getHerdrListHead`), never a second ranking and never a second `wl` spawn per bucket: one read path, buckets partitioned from the same ordered stream.
- Every sequential filter is applied unchanged to extended candidates: classification (producer-review gate, freshness/recency, risk/effort caps), dispatched-marker exclusion (24 h TTL), attempt budget, non-terminal cooldown, code-freeze split-by-skill, in-flight guard, and the review-queue depth hold. No filter is relaxed or reordered, and a gate-held candidate never becomes a nominee just because it is deeper.
- Cost is bounded and observable: the extension only runs when a bucket is unfilled, growth is geometric, rounds are capped, and the existing fail-open behaviour holds (an absent/`{ok:false}`/throwing extension leaves the pre-change result byte-identical and never blocks dispatch).
- A `nomineesFilledBeyondWindow` (or equivalent) signal is recorded on the check-in / decision-log entry naming which buckets needed the extension and how many extra items were read, so an operator can see a root being reached past its visible list.
- Tests: (a) a 20-item window whose buckets are fully gated but whose tail has one eligible `plan` and one eligible `implement` yields both nominees, in canonical order; (b) after a refused audit the same entry still dispatches its prep nominee — the fall-through the leader's phase-2 ladder already supports; (c) a tail with nothing eligible still resolves `noCandidate` with unchanged attribution; (d) the extension is not entered when the window already fills every bucket (no extra reads); (e) `wl` failure in the extension leaves the window result unchanged.
- Docs: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` states that the visible window bounds rendering only, and that buckets are filled from the whole ranked backlog. Update the "window is never widened to fill a bucket" statement in `downtime-worker.coordination.ts`.
- **Explicitly out of scope, recorded rather than silently absorbed:** (i) candidates held by the 24 h dispatched-marker or by a still-open in-flight pane stay invisible regardless of widening — separate items own those (they are why `RISE-0MWC9J1OD001CT26` and `RISE-0MW6M69LE004Z0QG` are not offered today); (ii) the leader's registered-root sweep (`downtimeWorklogRoots`) stays a separate, independent mechanism.

## Impact

Every project can offer its dispatcher a full set of buckets drawn from its whole backlog, so a root whose visible top 20 items are all audits no longer hands the leader an empty menu while its ready work waits below the fold.

## Users

- **As the producer**, I want each project's ready work to be reachable by the dispatcher even when it sits below the visible worklist, so projects with large backlogs stop appearing idle.
- **As an agent debugging a root that offers only audits**, I want the offer computation to explain that it widened, or that every candidate was gated.

## Supersedes / related work

- **WL-0MWDDHQON0015T3P** — tier-aware offers. Its AC3 ("the window is never widened to fill a bucket") is superseded by this item; a comment has been recorded on that item.
- **WL-0MW9XS0XR007K1TH** — made every work item a dispatch candidate; this item extends the same principle to the nominee buckets.
- **WL-0MVR8GDJ3008WY3Y / WL-0MW4ZOSD6004SAVD** — the registered-root sweep (a *cross-root* mechanism, currently unconfigured on this machine); independent of this change.
- **WL-0MWFIZ8H5005FVNN** (round-robin charge) and the audit-admission fix — the other two blockers in the 13 Nov dispatch starvation, on separate items.

## Evidence / key files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination.ts` — `computeMostImportantItem`, `scanOfferable(head.items, withNominees=true)`, `emitNominees`, and the whole-backlog loop that passes `withNominees=false`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts` — `fetchExtendedHerdrItems`, `fetchWholeBacklogTail`, `DOWNTIME_DISPATCH_EXTEND_MAX`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` — `orderAdmissibleOffers` (audit-drain → prep → implement) and the audit-budget `continue` that already falls through to the next nominee.
- `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-coordination.json` — live evidence of one-bucket entries.

Gap found in the follow-up tier-aware offers work (WL-0MWDDHQON0015T3P): 'every work item is a dispatch candidate' was applied to the single legacy offer only. The per-bucket nominees (`implement`/`audit`/`prep`) are a window-only partition, so a root whose visible top 20 items are all audits still offers only an audit.

Taken up by WL-0MWFJ8R1P005G1H1 — fill empty buckets from the whole ranked backlog via the same geometric extension this item introduced.

data.comment:
Offer-bucket widening: AC3 of this item ('a bucket empty in the window nominates nothing and the window is never widened to fill it') is superseded.

Live evidence (13 Nov 2026): the coordination file shows tce-the-rising, SorraAgents, tce-main-street and Tableau-Card-Engine each nominating only an `audit` bucket, while their backlogs below the 20-item sprint window hold eligible `implement`/`plan` work. With the audit tier refused machine-wide by the failing audit-availability read, those roots hand the leader an empty menu and dispatch nothing.

Superseding item: WL-0MWFJ8R1P005G1H1 — 'Downtime offers: fill empty buckets from the rest of the project backlog, not just the visible list'. AC1/AC2 (tier-aware nomination, per-offer attribution) remain in force; only the window-only restriction is replaced by a bounded whole-backlog extension.
